speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, can you describe the nature of your altered mentation, such as confusion or drowsiness, and do you have any history of diabetes or other chronic illnesses?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation, reporting fever without chills and rigors. He denies sore throat, abdominal pain, headache, loose stool, burning micturition, or seizures. Has a history of tics and is currently taking haloperidol.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of tics and current haloperidol use, I need to rule out drug-induced causes. Do you have any muscle stiffness, tremors, or difficulty moving, and have you recently started or changed the dose of your medication?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Fever and altered mentation. I also have Profuse sweating, Generalized rigidity, Confusion and disorientation, Ability to move all limbs, Normal deep tendon reflexes with bilateral downgoing plantar responses.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on your symptoms of fever, rigidity, altered mentation, and autonomic instability, I suspect Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome. REQUEST TEST: Creatine_Kinase.

speaker: Doctor
text: The markedly elevated creatine kinase confirms rhabdomyolysis, which, combined with your fever, rigidity, and altered mentation, is diagnostic of Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome. DIAGNOSIS READY: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome
